sections.title: A day, verb by verb
sections.content: Hungarian describes a typical day with a set of everyday verbs, several of them -ik verbs you already know the pattern for. felkelek (I get up), zuhanyozom (I shower), felöltözöm (I get dressed), reggelizem (I have breakfast), dolgozom (I work), ebédelek (I have lunch), vacsorázom (I have dinner), lefekszem (I lie down/go to bed), alszom (I sleep) — string a few together with commas or és and you already have a whole day.

items.english: In the morning I get up, shower, and have breakfast.
In the evening I go to bed early.

sections.content: felkel, ebédel and vacsorázik/zuhanyozik/reggelizik/lefekszik/alszik are just more present-tense verbs, conjugated exactly the way you already know — nothing new about the endings here, just new everyday vocabulary to put them to work on.
